chunks: And Zurarah said: Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام said:

“Amir al-Mu’minin عليه السلام came upon a group of people and saw them praying in the mosque, having let their cloaks hang down, so he said to them: ‘What is the matter with you that you have let your garments hang down as though you were Jews who have come out from their synagogue?’”
Meaning their synagogue, and [he was forbidding] your letting your garments hang down.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amir al-Mu’minin, Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ: the mosque, the place where the prayer was being performed
key_terms.بِيعَتَهُمْ: their synagogue or place of worship
key_terms.سَدَلُوا: they let hang down loosely or draped
key_terms.يَهُودُ: Jews, mentioned here in a comparative expression

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about letting garments hang down during salat?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام reproved a manner of dress during salat in the mosque, specifically the practice of sadl, letting garments hang loosely. It indicates a disliked or prohibited prayer posture in dress and frames the instruction as a distinction from the practice of others.
